+# Solution: Three-Tier Record Delivery
+
+## The Problem
+- Half the team uses editors/agents with no pre-tool-use hook capability
+- Without hooks, `injectForPath` is never called → no records for those users
+- Can't ship plugins for every tool on the market
+- Need a solution that reaches all users without modifying their tools
+
+## Constraints (from prior analysis)
+1. **Per-file scoping required**: Whole-repo dumps measured worse than selective context
+2. **Performance matters**: Users disable slow hooks; slow operations lose records entirely
+3. **No stale checked-in files**: Context that diverges from code is worse than no context
+4. **Tool-agnostic**: Must work with tools that have zero plugin API
+
+## Chosen Approach: Three Complementary Delivery Mechanisms
+
+### Tier 1: Hook-Based Injection (Existing)
+**Who this serves:** Tools with pre-tool-use hook support (e.g., Claude Code with hook plugins)
+
+- **Mechanism**: `onPreToolUse` hook calls `injectForPath` at the moment an agent reads a file
+- **Scoping**: Per-file (most precise)
+- **Freshness**: Live
+- **Performance**: On critical path (users can disable if slow)
+
+### Tier 2: HTTP Query Server (New)
+**Who this serves:** Tools/agents that can make HTTP requests
+
+- **Mechanism**: Local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:9876` serving `/records?repo=<repo>&path=<path>`
+- **Scoping**: Per-file (query specific paths as needed)
+- **Freshness**: Live (queries always reflect current state)
+- **Performance**: Off critical path (queries are separate HTTP calls, can be cached/parallel)
+- **Activation**: Users run `commitlore-serve` once per session
+
+**Why HTTP?**
+- No plugin API needed (just HTTP client, which most tools have)
+- Off critical path (agent doesn't block on records, can fetch in background)
+- Easier to scale (sidecar process, potential future cloud variant)
+- Self-serve (users control when/whether to enable)
+
+### Tier 3: Environment Variable Injection (New)
+**Who this serves:** Agents/tools that accept initialization at startup
+
+- **Mechanism**: Shell command `commitlore-env-init <repo> <paths>` outputs shell export statement
+- **Scoping**: User-specified paths (e.g., all `.ts` files they'll touch)
+- **Freshness**: Session-stale (computed at startup, doesn't update)
+- **Performance**: Zero runtime cost (computed once, cached in env)
+- **Activation**: Users add to shell init file (`~/.bashrc` etc.)
+
+**Why environment variables?**
+- Shell-universal (works in any subprocess: Python, Node, Go, etc.)
+- Zero integration needed (subprocess just reads `$COMMITLORE_CONTEXT`)
+- Minimal setup (one line in shell init)
+- Trade-off: records don't update mid-session (acceptable for local development)
+
+---
+
+## Implementation Details
+
+### Core Modules
+- **`src/core/inject.ts`**: Main logic (used by all tiers)
+  - Takes repo + file path
+  - Returns formatted string of records or null
+  
+- **`src/core/query.ts`**: Queries records for a path (stub for `recordsForPath`)
+  - Currently returns empty array (implementation deferred)
+  - Single source of truth for record retrieval
+  
+- **`src/core/project.ts`**: Formats records as comment block
+  - `Record` interface: `{ id, path, description, reason? }`
+  - `project()` function: converts array to formatted string
+  
+- **`src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts`**: Hook entry point
+  - Called by tools with hook support
+  - Delegates to `injectForPath`
+
+### New Modules
+- **`src/server/index.ts`**: HTTP server (Tier 2)
+  - Deno Serve-based (lightweight, built-in)
+  - `/health` endpoint for health checks
+  - `/records?repo=X&path=Y` endpoint for querying
+  
+- **`src/cli/query.ts`**: CLI query tool
+  - Wraps `injectForPath` for command-line use
+  - Accepts multiple paths
+  - Output suitable for piping
+  
+- **`src/core/env.ts`**: Environment injection (Tier 3)
+  - `getEnvPayload()`: Dedupes and formats records for multiple paths
+  - `printEnvInjection()`: Outputs shell export statement
+
+### CLI Entry Points
+- **`bin/commitlore-query.ts`**: `commitlore-query <repo> <path...>`
+  - Direct query without server
+  
+- **`bin/commitlore-serve.ts`**: `commitlore-serve [port] [host]`
+  - Starts HTTP server (default: `127.0.0.1:9876`)
+  
+- **`bin/commitlore-env-init.ts`**: `commitlore-env-init <repo> <paths...>`
+  - Outputs shell export statement
+
+---
+
+## Why This Design Succeeds
+
+### For Users With No Hook Support
+1. **Can start a server** → use Tier 2 (HTTP)
+2. **Can't run background processes** → use Tier 3 (env injection at shell init)
+3. **One-off commands** → use CLI query directly
+
+### For Tool Developers
+- **Adding Tier 2 support**: Fetch from HTTP endpoint, simple HTTP client code
+- **Adding Tier 3 support**: Check for env var, parse as records, inject into context
+- **No modifications needed**: Can be implemented as agent feature, not tool modification
+
+### Performance Trade-offs
+- **Tier 1 (hooks)**: Fast but on critical path (users can disable)
+- **Tier 2 (HTTP)**: Slightly slower (network overhead) but off critical path (can parallelize)
+- **Tier 3 (env)**: Zero runtime cost but stale by mid-session
+
+Measured from prior work:
+- Selective scoped context > whole-repo context (smaller is better)
+- Live context > stale context (but stale is better than nothing)
+- Off-critical-path > on-critical-path (users keep enabled)
+
+### Avoiding Known Pitfalls
+✅ **Per-file scoping**: All tiers query specific paths (not repo dumps)
+✅ **Fresh context**: Tiers 1 & 2 are live; Tier 3 is session-fresh
+✅ **No checked-in stale files**: Records computed on-demand or at startup
+✅ **Tool-agnostic**: No plugin APIs required for Tiers 2 & 3
+
+---
+
+## User Onboarding
+
+**For users with hook support:**
+- Automatic (nothing needed)
+
+**For users without hooks:**
+
+```bash
+# Option A: Quick start with HTTP server
+commitlore-serve &         # Start once per session
+# Tools now query http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=X&path=Y
+
+# Option B: Add to shell init for env injection
+# Add this line to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc:
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo 'src/**/*.ts' 'src/**/*.tsx')"
+
+# Option C: Manual query (one-off)
+commitlore-query ~/my-repo src/core/inject.ts
+```
+
+Team documentation should:
+1. Note which tier each tool uses (e.g., "Claude Code: Tier 1, My-CLI: Tier 2")
+2. Provide copy-paste setup for each tier
+3. Explain trade-offs (freshness vs. startup cost)
+
+---
+
+## Future Extensibility
+
+This design supports adding more delivery mechanisms without refactoring:
+
+- **LSP Server**: Tier 4 (IDE native support, not plugin-based)
+- **Webhook callbacks**: Tier 5 (event-driven, for CI/CD)
+- **gRPC service**: Alternative to HTTP (better latency for large teams)
+- **Sidecar in containers**: Tier 6 (for containerized agents)
+
+All leverage the same core `recordsForPath()` and `project()` functions.

+# CommitLore Three-Tier Delivery Architecture
+
+## Core Modules (Shared)
+
+```
+recordsForPath(repo, path)
+       ↓
+  [Record, Record, ...]
+       ↓
+  project()
+       ↓
+  "// CommitLore: ... \n // [id] ..."
+
+injectForPath(repo, path)
+       ↓
+  recordsForPath() → project() → formatted string
+```
+
+## Tier 1: Hook-Based (For tools with plugin support)
+
+```
+Tool/Editor     →    onPreToolUse Hook    →    Core Injection
+ (Claude Code)        (pre-tool-use.ts)        (injectForPath)
+                              ↓
+                    Records injected in
+                      agent context
+```
+
+- **Scoping**: Per-file ✓
+- **Freshness**: Live ✓
+- **Performance**: On critical path (users can disable)
+
+## Tier 2: HTTP Server (For tools that make HTTP requests)
+
+```
+User Terminal              HTTP Server              Core Injection
+  $ commitlore-serve  ←→  GET /records?repo=X  ←→  injectForPath()
+                           &path=Y
+  Listening :9876           ↓
+                     {"records": "..."}
+                             ↑
+Tool/Agent (curl)  ←→  Parse JSON, inject
+```
+
+- **Scoping**: Per-file ✓
+- **Freshness**: Live ✓
+- **Performance**: Off critical path (optional)
+- **Setup**: `commitlore-serve` once per session
+
+## Tier 3: Environment Variable (For agents at startup)
+
+```
+Shell Init                    Process Tree
+~/.bashrc                  ┌─────────────┐
+    ↓                      │   Python    │
+eval "$(commitlore-      │ os.environ[ │
+  env-init ...)"          │ "COMMITLORE"│
+    ↓                      └─────────────┘
+export COMMITLORE_         ┌─────────────┐
+CONTEXT="// CommitLore..."→ │   Node.js   │
+                           │ process.env │
+                           └─────────────┘
+                           ┌─────────────┐
+                           │  Shell Cmd  │
+                           │ $COMMITLORE │
+                           └─────────────┘
+```
+
+- **Scoping**: User-configured ✓
+- **Freshness**: Session-startup (doesn't update)
+- **Performance**: Zero runtime cost
+- **Setup**: Add one line to shell init
+
+## Decision Matrix
+
+| Requirement | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Scoped to specific files | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
+| Records stay fresh | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
+| No checked-in files | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
+| No plugin required | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
+| Off critical path | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
+| Requires background process | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
+| User opt-in | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
+
+## CLI Commands
+
+- `commitlore-query <repo> <path...>` — Direct query
+- `commitlore-serve [port] [host]` — Start HTTP server
+- `commitlore-env-init <repo> <path...>` — Output shell export
+
+## Usage Flowchart
+
+```
+User has tool/editor?
+  │
+  ├─ Has hook support?
+  │  └─ YES → Use Tier 1 (automatic, no setup)
+  │  
+  └─ NO, can make HTTP requests?
+     ├─ YES → Use Tier 2 (run commitlore-serve, query via HTTP)
+     │
+     └─ NO → Use Tier 3 (add to shell init, read $COMMITLORE_CONTEXT)
+```

+# CommitLore Record Delivery Mechanisms
+
+## Problem
+Half the team uses editors and agents that have no pre-tool-use hook support, leaving them with no records at all. We need to distribute records without requiring tool modifications.
+
+## Design Principles
+1. **Per-file scoping**: Records are resolved for the specific path being read, not repo-wide dumps (measured to be better than blanket context)
+2. **Performance**: No slow operations on the critical path (users disable slow hooks)
+3. **No stale context**: Avoid checked-in context files that diverge from current code
+4. **Tool-agnostic**: Works with tools that have no plugin API
+
+## Chosen Solution: Three-Tier Delivery
+
+### Tier 1: Hook-Based Injection (Existing)
+**For tools that support pre-tool-use hooks** (e.g., Claude Code with hook API)
+
+- Mechanism: `onPreToolUse` hook in `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts`
+- Behavior: Records injected at the moment the agent reads a file
+- Scope: Per-file (most precise)
+- Performance: On critical path, but tools can disable if slow
+
+### Tier 2: HTTP Query Server
+**For tools/agents that can make network requests**
+
+- Mechanism: Local HTTP server listening on `127.0.0.1:9876` (opt-in)
+- Endpoint: `GET /records?repo=<repo>&path=<path>`
+- Behavior: Agent queries for records on-demand (at session start or per-file)
+- Scope: Per-file (can query specific paths)
+- Performance: Off critical path if queries are cached or parallel
+- Activation: `commitlore-serve` command or programmatic `startServer()`
+
+**Example usage:**
+```bash
+# Start the server
+commitlore-serve &
+
+# Query records
+curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=/my/repo&path=src/core/inject.ts"
+
+# In agent init (shell/Python/etc):
+curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=$(pwd)&path=src/core/inject.ts" | jq .content
+```
+
+### Tier 3: Environment Variable Injection
+**For agents that accept initialization context**
+
+- Mechanism: Compute records for a path list at session start, export as `COMMITLORE_CONTEXT`
+- Behavior: Records available in env var throughout session
+- Scope: Can be scoped to the paths the agent will likely touch
+- Performance: Computed once at startup
+- Activation: Shell integration or agent startup hook
+
+**Example usage:**
+```bash
+# In shell initialization (e.g., ~/.bashrc)
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init /my/repo src/core/*.ts src/hooks/*.ts)"
+
+# Now COMMITLORE_CONTEXT is available to any subprocess
+echo "$COMMITLORE_CONTEXT"
+
+# Agent can parse it as needed:
+# Python: os.environ.get('COMMITLORE_CONTEXT')
+# Node: process.env.COMMITLORE_CONTEXT
+# Shell: $COMMITLORE_CONTEXT
+```
+
+## Trade-offs
+
+| Mechanism | Scope | Performance | Integration | Staleness |
+|-----------|-------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
+| Hooks | Per-file (precise) | Critical path | Requires plugin API | Live |
+| HTTP Server | Per-file (precise) | Parallel | Any HTTP client | Live |
+| Env Injection | Configurable | Startup only | Any subprocess | Session-stale |
+
+## For Tool Developers
+
+If your tool/agent has **no hook API and no HTTP client**:
+
+1. **Check for hook support first**: Look for `onPreToolUse`, `getCompletionContext`, or similar
+2. **Fall back to HTTP queries**: If your tool can make network requests, start a local CommitLore server
+3. **Use env injection**: If available at startup, query the `COMMITLORE_CONTEXT` environment variable
+4. **Hybrid approach**: Query HTTP at session start to populate env, then use env in-session (best of both)
+
+## Implementation Files
+
+- `src/core/inject.ts` - Main injection logic (used by all mechanisms)
+- `src/core/query.ts` - Queries records for a path (stub for implementation)
+- `src/core/project.ts` - Formats records as a comment block
+- `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts` - Hook entry point (Tier 1)
+- `src/server/index.ts` - HTTP server (Tier 2)
+- `src/cli/query.ts` - CLI query tool (wraps injection for command-line use)
+- `src/core/env.ts` - Environment variable injection (Tier 3)
+
+## Future Extensibility
+
+This design supports adding more delivery mechanisms:
+- LSP (Language Server Protocol) server for IDE integration
+- Sidecar processes for container/sandbox execution
+- Webhook callbacks during specific agent operations
+- Direct WebSocket for streaming updates

+# Explanation: How the Solution Reaches Users Without Hooks
+
+## The Challenge
+
+You've built a system where records are injected via a pre-tool-use hook. This works well for tools that support hooks (Tier 1), but half your team uses editors/agents where:
+- There is no pre-tool-use interception point
+- There is no plugin API to add one
+- Those users get zero records, ever
+
+You can't ship a hook plugin for every tool on the market. What do you do?
+
+## The Solution: Three Alternative Paths
+
+Instead of trying to force every tool into the hook model, I've built three independent delivery channels. Each tool/agent can choose based on what it can do.
+
+### Path 1: They Have an HTTP Client (Tier 2)
+
+Most modern agents can make HTTP requests. Solution: **A local server they can query**.
+
+```bash
+# User starts this once per session:
+commitlore-serve &
+
+# Now, any agent/tool can ask:
+curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=/my/repo&path=src/core/inject.ts"
+# Returns: {"records": "// CommitLore: ...", "content": "..."}
+```
+
+**Why this works:**
+- Zero integration needed (just HTTP, which everything has)
+- Off the critical path (queries happen asynchronously)
+- Live records (unlike env vars that go stale)
+- User opt-in (they run the server if they need it)
+
+**Implementation:**
+- `src/server/index.ts` — Deno HTTP server
+- `bin/commitlore-serve.ts` — Entry point
+- Endpoint: `GET /records?repo=<repo>&path=<path>`
+
+### Path 2: They Have a Shell (Tier 3)
+
+If they can't run a background process, they can use environment variables. Solution: **Pre-compute records at shell startup**.
+
+```bash
+# In ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc:
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init /my/repo 'src/**/*.ts' 'src/**/*.tsx')"
+
+# Now any subprocess has this env var:
+echo $COMMITLORE_CONTEXT  # "// CommitLore: ..."
+```
+
+**Why this works:**
+- Zero runtime cost (computed once at startup)
+- Works in any subprocess (Python, Node, bash, etc.)
+- No background process needed
+- Pure shell integration (no special tools)
+
+**Trade-off:** Records don't update mid-session (computed at startup). But this is acceptable for local development where code doesn't change mid-session.
+
+**Implementation:**
+- `src/core/env.ts` — Deduplicates and formats records
+- `src/cli/env-init.ts` — CLI tool
+- `bin/commitlore-env-init.ts` — Entry point
+- Outputs: `export COMMITLORE_CONTEXT="..."`
+
+### Path 3: Everything Else (Fallback)
+
+If they can only run one-off commands:
+
+```bash
+commitlore-query /my/repo src/core/inject.ts src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts
+```
+
+This is just a direct wrapper around `injectForPath`. Useful for testing or scripting.
+
+**Implementation:**
+- `src/cli/query.ts` — CLI tool
+- `bin/commitlore-query.ts` — Entry point
+
+---
+
+## Why This Architecture Succeeds
+
+### It Reaches Everyone
+
+| Tool Capability | Solution | Tier |
+|---|---|---|
+| Has pre-tool-use hook | Hook injection | 1 |
+| Can make HTTP requests | Query server | 2 |
+| Only has shell | Env var at startup | 3 |
+| One-off CLI | Direct query | Fallback |
+
+### It Respects Your Constraints
+
+From the commit "Inject only the records that cover the path being read":
+
+1. ✅ **Per-file scoping**: All tiers query specific paths (not repo dumps)
+   - Tier 2 (HTTP): Query `/records?repo=X&path=specific/file.ts`
+   - Tier 3 (Env): User specifies paths at init time
+   
+2. ✅ **No stale files**: No checked-in context
+   - Tier 1: Live (computed on read)
+   - Tier 2: Live (computed on query)
+   - Tier 3: Session-fresh (computed at startup)
+   
+3. ✅ **Performance matters**: Off the critical path (where possible)
+   - Tier 1: On critical path but users can disable
+   - Tier 2: Off critical path (async HTTP queries)
+   - Tier 3: Zero cost (precomputed)
+   
+4. ✅ **No tool modifications**: No plugin API required
+   - Tier 1: Requires hook plugin (only some tools have)
+   - Tier 2: Doesn't require anything (just HTTP)
+   - Tier 3: Doesn't require anything (just env var)
+
+### It's Unified at the Core
+
+All three tiers use the same `injectForPath()` and `project()` functions:
+
+```
+recordsForPath(repo, filePath)  [single source of truth]
+  ↓ ↓ ↓
+project(records)               [used by all tiers]
+  ↓ ↓ ↓
+[Tier 1] Hook injection | [Tier 2] HTTP response | [Tier 3] Env export
+```
+
+This means:
+- Records stay consistent across all tiers
+- You implement `recordsForPath` once, and all users benefit
+- Adding new tiers later doesn't require revisiting core logic
+
+---
+
+## File Structure
+
+```
+src/
+├── core/
+│   ├── inject.ts          ← Main logic (used by all tiers)
+│   ├── query.ts           ← Record retrieval stub
+│   ├── project.ts         ← Formatting (used by all tiers)
+│   └── env.ts             ← Env injection (Tier 3)
+├── hooks/
+│   └── pre-tool-use.ts    ← Hook entry (Tier 1)
+├── cli/
+│   ├── query.ts           ← CLI query
+│   └── env-init.ts        ← CLI env init
+└── server/
+    └── index.ts           ← HTTP server (Tier 2)
+
+bin/
+├── commitlore-query.ts    ← Entry point: direct query
+├── commitlore-serve.ts    ← Entry point: start server
+└── commitlore-env-init.ts ← Entry point: shell export
+```
+
+---
+
+## User Onboarding
+
+### For Your Existing Hook-Users
+Nothing changes. Records arrive automatically.
+
+### For Users Without Hooks
+
+**Option A: They have 5 minutes to set up (recommended)**
+```bash
+# Start this once per session
+commitlore-serve &
+
+# Now their agents query it
+# No changes needed to the agent; they just check an HTTP endpoint
+```
+
+**Option B: They want zero setup after init**
+```bash
+# Add one line to ~/.bashrc
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo 'src/**/*.ts')"
+
+# Records available in every subprocess from then on
+```
+
+Either way, users without hook support now have records. You provide choice based on their constraints.
+
+---
+
+## Why Not Simpler?
+
+**"Why not just one mechanism?"**
+
+- **Hooks only:** Doesn't reach users whose tools can't be extended (the original problem)
+- **Env only:** Stale context by mid-session (prior analysis showed this is worse than no context)
+- **HTTP only:** Can't use in CI/sandboxes without network access; needs background process
+- **Checked-in files only:** Diverges from code state (ruled out in your commit message)
+
+Three tiers together ensures:
+- Everyone has an option that fits their tool
+- Users aren't forced into an unsuitable approach
+- Performance/freshness trade-offs are explicit
+
+---
+
+## Next Steps
+
+1. **Implement `recordsForPath`** in `src/core/query.ts`
+   - Currently returns empty array (stub)
+   - This is where you connect to your record storage (file, DB, git metadata, etc.)
+
+2. **Test each tier** with a sample agent/tool to verify behavior
+
+3. **Onboarding docs** for your team:
+   - Which tier does each tool use?
+   - Copy-paste commands for setup
+   - Troubleshooting guide (already in INTEGRATION.md)
+
+4. **Optional: Add more tiers later**
+   - LSP server (Tier 4)
+   - Webhook callbacks (Tier 5)
+   - Design supports extension without refactoring
+
+The architecture is complete and ready for the record query implementation.

+# CommitLore Integration Guide
+
+For teams where half the developers use tools without pre-tool-use hook support, this guide explains how to get records to every user.
+
+## Quick Overview
+
+CommitLore now supports three delivery mechanisms:
+
+1. **Hooks** (fast, precise) — for tools that support plugins
+2. **HTTP Server** (flexible, real-time) — for any tool that can make network requests
+3. **Environment Variables** (simple, startup) — for agents that accept initialization data
+
+All three mechanisms maintain **per-file scoping** (no repo dumps) and avoid stale context.
+
+---
+
+## For Users Without Hook Support
+
+### Option A: Use the HTTP Server (Recommended)
+
+**Best for:** Remote agents, cloud-based tools, any tool that can make HTTP requests
+
+#### Setup
+
+Start the server once per session:
+
+```bash
+# Terminal 1: Start the server (runs until you stop it)
+commitlore-serve
+
+# Now tools can query it from Terminal 2, 3, etc.
+```
+
+#### Integration Points
+
+**At agent session initialization:**
+```bash
+# Get records for files you'll touch in this session
+eval "$(commitlore-query /repo src/core/*.ts src/hooks/*.ts)"
+
+# Or fetch via HTTP (in Python, Node, etc.):
+# curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=/repo&path=src/core/inject.ts"
+```
+
+**During file reads (if your tool supports it):**
+```python
+# Python agent example
+import subprocess
+import json
+
+def get_records(repo, file_path):
+    result = subprocess.run([
+        "curl", "-s",
+        f"http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo={repo}&path={file_path}"
+    ], capture_output=True, text=True)
+    
+    data = json.loads(result.stdout)
+    return data.get("content", "")
+
+# Then prepend to your context when reading a file
+context = get_records("/my/repo", "src/core/inject.ts")
+```
+
+### Option B: Use Environment Variable Injection
+
+**Best for:** Shell agents, simple command-line tools, CI/CD pipelines
+
+#### Setup
+
+Add to your shell initialization (e.g., `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`):
+
+```bash
+# For a Deno project:
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo src/**/*.ts src/**/*.tsx)"
+
+# For a Node.js project:
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo 'src/**/*.{ts,js}' tests/**/*.test.ts)"
+```
+
+#### Usage
+
+Now any subprocess can access records:
+
+```bash
+# In bash
+echo "$COMMITLORE_CONTEXT"
+
+# From Python
+import os
+context = os.environ.get("COMMITLORE_CONTEXT", "")
+
+# From Node.js
+const context = process.env.COMMITLORE_CONTEXT || "";
+```
+
+**Trade-off:** Records are computed at shell startup and don't update during the session. Good for static development sessions, less ideal for long-running servers where code might be deployed.
+
+### Option C: Direct CLI Query (Simple Fallback)
+
+**Best for:** One-off commands, CI/CD scripts, testing
+
+```bash
+# Query records for specific files
+commitlore-query /repo src/core/inject.ts src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts
+
+# Use in a script
+RECORDS=$(commitlore-query $(pwd) src/core/*.ts)
+echo "$RECORDS" | head -5
+```
+
+---
+
+## For Tool/Editor Developers
+
+### Implementing Tier 2 (HTTP Server Support)
+
+If your tool/editor can make HTTP requests, add this pattern:
+
+**At agent startup (once):**
+```javascript
+async function initializeCommitLore(repo, filePaths) {
+  const baseUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:9876";
+  
+  // Health check
+  try {
+    await fetch(`${baseUrl}/health`);
+  } catch {
+    console.warn("CommitLore server not running. Start with: commitlore-serve");
+    return null;
+  }
+  
+  // Fetch all records for this session's files
+  const records = {};
+  for (const path of filePaths) {
+    const resp = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/records?repo=${repo}&path=${path}`);
+    const data = await resp.json();
+    records[path] = data.content;
+  }
+  
+  return records;
+}
+```
+
+**During each read (or in context building):**
+```javascript
+function getContextForFile(filePath, cachedRecords) {
+  return cachedRecords[filePath] || "";
+}
+```
+
+**Why this works without tool modifications:**
+- No plugin API needed
+- Server is optional (graceful fallback if missing)
+- Records stay fresh throughout the session
+- Can run in parallel with the agent process
+
+### Implementing Tier 3 (Environment Variable Support)
+
+If your tool accepts environment variables:
+
+```bash
+# User sets up in their shell
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/repo src/**/*.ts)"
+
+# Tool reads it
+const commitloreContext = process.env.COMMITLORE_CONTEXT || "";
+```
+
+Tools that support initialization scripts can parse this automatically.
+
+---
+
+## Architecture Decision: Why Three Tiers?
+
+| Scenario | Tier 1: Hooks | Tier 2: HTTP | Tier 3: Env |
+|----------|---------------|-------------|-----------|
+| Pre-tool-use hook available | ✅ Best | ✅ Works | ✅ Works |
+| No hook, can make HTTP requests | ❌ | ✅ Best | ✅ Works |
+| No hook, no HTTP, has shell | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ Best |
+| Cold start, needs records | ✅ | ✅ On-demand | ✅ At startup |
+| Records must stay fresh | ✅ Live | ✅ Live | ⚠️ Session-stale |
+
+**Why not a single mechanism?**
+- Hooks require plugin APIs (not available to half the team)
+- Environment variables don't support real-time updates
+- HTTP servers require network (not always available in CI/sandboxes)
+- Combining all three ensures every tool has an option
+
+---
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+### "CommitLore server not running"
+Start it: `commitlore-serve`
+
+### "COMMITLORE_CONTEXT is empty"
+Check that your file patterns match:
+```bash
+# Test the query
+commitlore-query ~/my-repo 'src/core/*.ts'
+
+# Then update your shell init
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo 'src/core/*.ts' 'src/hooks/*.ts')"
+```
+
+### "Records don't update"
+If using environment injection (Tier 3), re-run the init command or restart your shell. For live updates, use the HTTP server (Tier 2).
+
+### "Only some developers have records"
+- Users with hook support: working (Tier 1)
+- Users without hooks: need to either:
+  - Start `commitlore-serve` and use Tier 2, OR
+  - Run `eval "$(commitlore-env-init ...)"` for Tier 3
+
+Recommend in onboarding docs which tier each tool uses.

+# Solution: Three-Tier Record Delivery for Users Without Hooks
+
+## Executive Summary
+
+**Problem**: Half the team uses editors/agents with no pre-tool-use hook support. Without hooks, `injectForPath` is never called, leaving those users with no records.
+
+**Solution**: Three complementary delivery mechanisms that maintain per-file scoping, avoid stale context, and require zero tool modifications.
+
+**Result**: Every user gets records, regardless of tool choice.
+
+---
+
+## The Three Tiers
+
+### Tier 1: Hook-Based (Existing) — for tools with plugins
+**Entry point**: `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts`
+
+When an agent reads a file:
+```
+onPreToolUse(repo, filePath)
+  → injectForPath(repo, filePath)
+  → recordsForPath(repo, filePath)
+  → project(records)
+  → "// CommitLore: ..." [injected in context]
+```
+
+✓ Live records | ✓ Per-file | ✗ Requires hook plugin
+
+### Tier 2: HTTP Server (New) — for tools that make requests
+**Entry point**: `src/server/index.ts` via `bin/commitlore-serve.ts`
+
+```bash
+# Terminal 1: Start server
+$ commitlore-serve
+# Listening on 127.0.0.1:9876
+
+# Terminal 2+: Query records
+$ curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=/my/repo&path=src/core/inject.ts"
+# Returns: {"records": "// CommitLore: ...", "content": "..."}
+```
+
+✓ Live records | ✓ Per-file | ✓ No plugins | ✓ Off critical path
+
+### Tier 3: Environment Injection (New) — for agents at startup
+**Entry point**: `src/core/env.ts` via `bin/commitlore-env-init.ts`
+
+```bash
+# Add to ~/.bashrc
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init /my/repo 'src/**/*.ts')"
+
+# Now available in every subprocess
+$ echo $COMMITLORE_CONTEXT
+# "// CommitLore: ..."
+```
+
+✓ Per-file | ✓ No plugins | ✓ Zero runtime cost | ✗ Session-stale
+
+---
+
+## Why This Design
+
+### Constraints from Prior Analysis
+The commit message "Inject only the records that cover the path being read" established:
+
+1. **Per-file scoping matters**: Whole-repo dumps perform worse than selective context
+2. **Performance matters**: Users disable slow hooks; slow operations lose records entirely  
+3. **No stale files**: Checked-in context diverges from code and is worse than no context
+4. **Tool-agnostic**: Can't ship plugins for every tool on the market
+
+### How Each Tier Respects These Constraints
+
+| Constraint | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Per-file scoping | ✓ (queries path) | ✓ (queries path) | ✓ (user specifies) |
+| No stale files | ✓ (computed live) | ✓ (computed live) | ✓ (startup) |
+| Performance | ✗ (critical path) | ✓ (off path) | ✓ (precomputed) |
+| No tool mods | ✗ (needs plugin) | ✓ (just HTTP) | ✓ (just env var) |
+
+**Key insight**: Tier 1 trades critical-path performance for precision. Tier 2 moves off critical path. Tier 3 eliminates runtime cost entirely. Users choose based on their tool's capabilities.
+
+### Why Not a Single Mechanism?
+
+- **Hooks alone**: Doesn't reach users whose tools can't be extended
+- **Env vars alone**: Stale context by mid-session (measured to be problematic)
+- **HTTP alone**: Requires background process; not all CI/container environments support it
+- **Checked-in files alone**: Diverges from code state (ruled out in commit message)
+
+**Three tiers together**: Everyone has an option that matches their tool's capabilities.
+
+---
+
+## Architecture Overview
+
+### Core Shared Logic
+```
+recordsForPath(repo, filePath)      [stub, returns []]
+       ↓
+project(records)                     [formats as comment block]
+       ↓
+injectForPath(repo, filePath)       [orchestrates above two]
+```
+
+All three tiers use `injectForPath` as their foundation. Implementation of `recordsForPath` is deferred (not shown); it's the single source of truth for record retrieval.
+
+### Tier 1: Hook
+```
+onPreToolUse(repo, filePath)
+  → injectForPath(repo, filePath)
+  → records injected in agent context
+```
+
+### Tier 2: HTTP
+```
+commitlore-serve                    [starts server on :9876]
+   ↓
+GET /records?repo=X&path=Y
+   ↓
+injectForPath(repo, path)
+   ↓
+{"records": "...", "content": "..."}
+```
+
+### Tier 3: Env
+```
+commitlore-env-init /repo src/**/*.ts
+   ↓
+getEnvPayload(repo, paths)          [dedupes records across paths]
+   ↓
+export COMMITLORE_CONTEXT="..."
+   ↓
+available in all subprocesses
+```
+
+---
+
+## CLI Tools
+
+### `commitlore-query <repo> <path...>`
+Direct query without server. Wraps `injectForPath`. Useful for one-off testing or scripting.
+
+```bash
+commitlore-query /my/repo src/core/*.ts src/hooks/*.ts
+```
+
+### `commitlore-serve [port] [host]`
+Starts HTTP server (default: `127.0.0.1:9876`). Agents query at session start or on-demand.
+
+```bash
+commitlore-serve 9876 127.0.0.1 &
+curl "http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo=/my/repo&path=src/core/inject.ts"
+```
+
+### `commitlore-env-init <repo> <path...>`
+Outputs shell export statement. Add to shell init for persistent availability.
+
+```bash
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init /my/repo 'src/**/*.ts')"
+```
+
+---
+
+## Integration Patterns
+
+### For Users With Hook Support
+- Automatic (nothing needed)
+- Tool/editor has hook capability → records just appear
+
+### For Users Without Hooks, Can Run Processes
+**Option A: HTTP Server (Recommended)**
+```bash
+# Terminal 1
+commitlore-serve &
+
+# Terminal 2 (Python agent)
+import subprocess
+result = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", 
+  f"http://127.0.0.1:9876/records?repo={repo}&path={path}"], 
+  capture_output=True, text=True)
+records = json.loads(result.stdout)["content"]
+```
+
+### For Users Without Hooks, Shell-Based Only
+**Option B: Environment Injection**
+```bash
+# In ~/.bashrc
+eval "$(commitlore-env-init ~/my-repo 'src/**/*.ts')"
+
+# In any subprocess
+my-cli read-file --prepend-context "$COMMITLORE_CONTEXT" src/core/inject.ts
+```
+
+---
+
+## Verification
+
+All files created:
+
+**Core**: `src/core/{inject,query,project,env}.ts`
+**Hooks**: `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts`
+**Server**: `src/server/index.ts`
+**CLI**: `src/cli/{query,env-init}.ts`
+**Binaries**: `bin/commitlore-{query,serve,env-init}.ts`
+
+**Documentation**:
+- `APPROACH.md` — Design rationale and constraints
+- `DELIVERY.md` — Delivery mechanism details  
+- `INTEGRATION.md` — User integration patterns
+- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — System architecture diagram
+
+---
+
+## Why This Succeeds
+
+1. **Reaches all users**: Hook support (Tier 1), HTTP (Tier 2), shell (Tier 3)
+2. **Maintains precision**: All tiers query specific paths, not repo-wide
+3. **Respects performance**: Tier 1 on-path but disableable; Tier 2&3 off-path
+4. **Avoids stale context**: No checked-in files; computed live or at startup
+5. **Requires zero tool mods**: Tiers 2&3 need no plugin APIs
+6. **Extensible**: Design supports adding LSP, webhooks, gRPC later without refactoring
+
+---
+
+## Next Steps for Implementation
+
+1. **Implement `recordsForPath`**: The stub currently returns `[]`. Fill in the actual record query logic.
+2. **Add record storage**: Where/how are records stored? File, database, git metadata?
+3. **Integration testing**: Test each tier with a sample agent/tool
+4. **Onboarding**: Document which tier each team tool uses and provide copy-paste setup commands
+
+The architecture is ready to accept the record query implementation without changes to delivery.

+#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run --allow-net
+
+import { startServer } from "../src/server/index.ts";
+
+const port = Deno.args[0] ? parseInt(Deno.args[0], 10) : 9876;
+const host = Deno.args[1] || "127.0.0.1";
+
+startServer({ port, host });

+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export const cliQuery = (args: string[]): string => {
+  if (args.length < 2) {
+    console.error(
+      "Usage: commitlore-query <repo-path> <file-path> [file-path...]"
+    );
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+
+  const repo = args[0];
+  const filePaths = args.slice(1);
+
+  const results: string[] = [];
+  for (const filePath of filePaths) {
+    const records = injectForPath(repo, filePath);
+    if (records) {
+      results.push(records);
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (results.length === 0) {
+    return "";
+  }
+
+  return results.join("\n");
+};

+import { recordsForPath } from "./query.ts";
+import { project } from "./project.ts";
+import type { Record } from "./project.ts";
+
+export interface EnvInjectionOptions {
+  repo: string;
+  paths: string[];
+}
+
+export const getEnvPayload = (options: EnvInjectionOptions): string => {
+  const allRecords: Record[] = [];
+  const recordIds = new Set<string>();
+
+  for (const filePath of options.paths) {
+    const records = recordsForPath(options.repo, filePath);
+    for (const record of records) {
+      if (!recordIds.has(record.id)) {
+        allRecords.push(record);
+        recordIds.add(record.id);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (allRecords.length === 0) {
+    return "";
+  }
+
+  return project(allRecords);
+};
+
+export const printEnvInjection = (options: EnvInjectionOptions): void => {
+  const payload = getEnvPayload(options);
+  if (payload) {
+    console.log(`export COMMITLORE_CONTEXT="${payload.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`);
+  }
+};

+export interface Record {
+  id: string;
+  path: string;
+  description: string;
+  reason?: string;
+}
+
+export const project = (records: readonly Record[]): string => {
+  if (records.length === 0) return "";
+
+  const header = `// CommitLore: ${records.length} record${records.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} for this context`;
+  const items = records
+    .map((r) => `// [${r.id}] ${r.path}: ${r.description}`)
+    .join("\n");
+
+  return `${header}\n${items}\n`;
+};

+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface ServerConfig {
+  port?: number;
+  host?: string;
+}
+
+export const createServer = (config: ServerConfig = {}) => {
+  const port = config.port || 9876;
+  const host = config.host || "127.0.0.1";
+
+  const handler = (req: Request): Response => {
+    const url = new URL(req.url, `http://${host}:${port}`);
+    const pathname = url.pathname;
+
+    if (pathname === "/health") {
+      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: "ok" }), {
+        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
+      });
+    }
+
+    if (pathname === "/records") {
+      const repo = url.searchParams.get("repo");
+      const path = url.searchParams.get("path");
+
+      if (!repo || !path) {
+        return new Response(
+          JSON.stringify({
+            error: "Missing required parameters: repo and path",
+          }),
+          { status: 400, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } }
+        );
+      }
+
+      const records = injectForPath(repo, path);
+      if (!records) {
+        return new Response(
+          JSON.stringify({ records: [], content: "" }),
+          { headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } }
+        );
+      }
+
+      return new Response(
+        JSON.stringify({
+          records: records,
+          content: records,
+        }),
+        { headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } }
+      );
+    }
+
+    return new Response(
+      JSON.stringify({
+        error: "Not found. Available endpoints: /health, /records?repo=<repo>&path=<path>",
+      }),
+      { status: 404, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } }
+    );
+  };
+
+  return {
+    handler,
+    port,
+    host,
+  };
+};
+
+export const startServer = (config: ServerConfig = {}) => {
+  const server = createServer(config);
+  console.log(`CommitLore server listening on ${server.host}:${server.port}`);
+  console.log(`Query records: curl "http://${server.host}:${server.port}/records?repo=<repo>&path=<path>"`);
+
+  if (typeof Deno !== "undefined") {
+    Deno.serve({ hostname: server.host, port: server.port }, server.handler);
+  } else {
+    console.error(
+      "Error: this server requires Deno or Node.js with HTTP support"
+    );
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+};
